_note: Additions made in the v54 build (10 Nov 2026): 50 nodes and 102 ties (Wexner and New Albany, the Maxwell and Giuffre cases and their judges, law firms, banks, the Senate Finance report, DP World). Each new tie keeps the refs it was built with.

nodes.name: Joseph Recarey
nodes.note: Lead Palm Beach Police detective on the 2005–06 Epstein investigation and writer of most of the case reports (Julie K. Brown). Died May 2018.

nodes.name: Haley Robson
nodes.note: Named in the Palm Beach police affidavits as having brought girls to Epstein's house in 2005, including a 14-year-old. She was a teenager herself when first approached, told police she brought six girls, and denies wrongdoing. Police reported probable cause as to her; the charging outcome was not checked.

nodes.name: C.O.U.Q. Foundation
nodes.note: Epstein charity; Darren Indyke was its vice president (Crimson). Tax filings reported by the Miami Herald and Jewish Insider show gifts of $15,000 (≈ $26,000 today) to the Jewish National Fund (Jun 2005), $25,000 (≈ $43,000 today) to Friends of the IDF (Mar 2005) and $100,000 (≈ $171,000 today) to the Columbus Jewish Foundation (May 2003), among many gifts to schools, synagogues, universities and medical charities. Some listed recipients told NBC News they never received the gifts. Not a finding about any recipient.

nodes.name: Jeffrey Epstein VI Foundation
nodes.note: Name on Epstein's science-philanthropy press releases. NBC reported its last tax filing was for 2002. Its releases claimed $30 million (≈ $56 million today) for Harvard's Program for Evolutionary Dynamics (BuzzFeed); Harvard and some recipients disputed or did not confirm gift sizes.

nodes.name: Jewish National Fund (recipient of a C.O.U.Q. gift)
nodes.note: Jewish institution that received a $15,000 (≈ $26,000 today) C.O.U.Q. gift in Jun 2005, per tax filings reported by Jewish Insider. Appears as a landowner node in the Road to 1948 map. A gift to a charity is not evidence of any role in Epstein's crimes.

nodes.name: Friends of the IDF
nodes.note: US charity that received $25,000 (≈ $43,000 today) from C.O.U.Q. in Mar 2005, per tax filings reported by Jewish Insider.

nodes.name: Columbus Jewish Foundation
nodes.note: Ohio foundation that received $100,000 (≈ $181,000 today) from C.O.U.Q. in May 2003, per tax filings reported by Jewish Insider.

nodes.name: United States v. Maxwell (20 Cr. 330, SDNY)
nodes.note: Indictment unsealed 29 Jun 2020. Maxwell convicted Dec 2021 and sentenced 28 Jun 2022 to 20 years. Second Circuit affirmed 17 Sep 2024; Supreme Court denied review 6 Oct 2025. Later rulings concern release of grand-jury material and the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

nodes.name: Giuffre v. Maxwell (15-cv-7433, SDNY)
nodes.note: Defamation suit by Virginia Giuffre, since settled. Documents sealed on Judge Sweet's order were reviewed and unsealed by Judge Preska from Dec 2019 after the Second Circuit remand; names in the unsealed documents were released from 1 Jan 2024. Miami Herald and Julie K. Brown were intervenors.

nodes.name: Judge Alison Nathan
nodes.note: Presided over the Maxwell trial (conviction 2021) and sentenced her (2022); later elevated to the Second Circuit.

nodes.name: Judge Paul Engelmayer
nodes.note: Took over the Maxwell case after Nathan's elevation; ruled on DOJ's motions to unseal grand-jury material (Dec 2025) and on lawmakers' bid to attach Epstein-files demands to the case (Jan 2026).

nodes.name: Judge Loretta Preska
nodes.note: Took over Giuffre v. Maxwell after Judge Sweet's death and ordered documents and names unsealed (2019–2024).

nodes.name: Judge Robert W. Sweet
nodes.note: Sentenced Steven Hoffenberg to 20 years in 1997 and originally presided over Giuffre v. Maxwell, sealing its documents. Died 2019.

nodes.name: Towers Financial Corporation
nodes.note: Manhattan debt-collection company that ran a Ponzi scheme 1988–93; SEC civil action Feb 1993, bankruptcy Mar 1993. Hoffenberg pleaded guilty 1995 and was sentenced 1997 to 20 years, with restitution of about $463–475 million (≈ $961 million–986 million today) in 1997 (sources differ). Epstein was hired in 1987 as a consultant at $25,000 (≈ $73,000 today) a month for about six years; he was never charged. Hoffenberg's 2019 claim that Epstein was an 'uncharged co-conspirator' is an allegation.

nodes.name: Doug Band
nodes.note: Senior aide to Bill Clinton, 2002–12. Appears on 2002 flights with Epstein and Clinton (flight manifests, as reported). Said in 2020 that he met Epstein in 2002 and urged Clinton to distance himself, and that Clinton visited Little St. James in Jan 2003. Emails with Maxwell 2002–06 reported; questioned by House Oversight (as reported). He denies any improper relationship.

nodes.name: The New Albany Company
nodes.note: Development firm Les Wexner co-founded in the 1980s that built New Albany, Ohio. Epstein was named a company president in a 1998 state filing (reported via WCMH-TV). The company says it, not Wexner personally, is the city's development partner.

nodes.name: New Albany, Ohio
nodes.note: Columbus suburb planned around the Wexner estate. Records show Epstein bought a house there in 1994, about half a mile from the Wexner home.

nodes.name: The Wexner Foundation
nodes.note: Foundation Les and Abigail Wexner created to support Jewish communities. Epstein was appointed to it; the foundation has said Epstein had no contact with its staff after September 2007.

nodes.name: Ohio State University
nodes.note: Wexner's alma mater, where he served two stints as trustee and where his name is on the medical center (2012, $100M gift), an arts center and a football complex. Naming-review requests are pending.

nodes.name: Columbus Partnership
nodes.note: Central Ohio civic-leadership nonprofit Wexner co-founded.

nodes.name: Robert Sprague
nodes.note: Ohio State Treasurer. Sent a donation matching the $23,000 the Wexners gave his 2022 campaign to a housing-services group after the Epstein deposition.

nodes.name: Kirkland & Ellis
nodes.note: Law firm that represented Epstein on the 2008 plea deal, media disputes and a hedge-fund suit; Epstein paid it more than $3.1M between 2008 and 2011. Starr and Lefkowitz were its lawyers; Alexander Acosta had been a Kirkland litigator before the Labor Department.

nodes.name: Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison
nodes.note: Law firm led by Brad Karp. The firm says it was adverse to Epstein and never represented him; Karp's contact grew out of representing Leon Black in a fee dispute. Emails show Karp reviewing Epstein's plea-deal strategy in 2019 and discussing Ruemmler's career.

nodes.name: Hogan Lovells
nodes.note: Law firm that discussed a job for Kathryn Ruemmler in 2015; she forwarded the exchange to Epstein.

nodes.name: Martin Weinberg
nodes.note: Boston defense lawyer on Epstein's legal team; part of the July 2019 team that argued the 2008 non-prosecution agreement could not be reopened.

nodes.name: DP World
nodes.note: Dubai-owned global port and logistics operator led for years by Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem. After the January 2026 DOJ release he resigned (13 Feb 2026); Essa Kazim became chairman and Yuvraj Narayan group CEO. UK development finance agency and Canada's La Caisse paused new investment.

nodes.name: Essa Kazim
nodes.note: Governor of the Dubai International Financial Centre, named DP World chairman on 13 Feb 2026.

nodes.name: Yuvraj Narayan
nodes.note: DP World's former CFO, named group CEO on 13 Feb 2026.

nodes.name: British International Investment
nodes.note: UK development finance institution reported to have suspended new investment with DP World over the Epstein ties.

nodes.name: La Caisse (CDPQ)
nodes.note: Quebec pension fund that paused new DP World investment, then said DP World had taken appropriate measures and it would work with the new leadership.

nodes.name: Fidelity Investments
nodes.note: Subpoenaed in July 2020 by USVI Attorney General Denise George for records on Epstein and more than 30 linked entities. A subpoena is not proof of an account.

nodes.name: Northern Trust International Banking Corp.
nodes.note: Subpoenaed in July 2020 by the USVI Attorney General in the Epstein estate case. A subpoena is not proof of an account.

nodes.name: Silicon Valley Bank
nodes.note: Subpoenaed in July 2020 by the USVI Attorney General in the Epstein estate case. A subpoena is not proof of an account.

nodes.name: BMO (Bank of Montreal)
nodes.note: Trustee bank on the AP Narrows Holding LP account already in the map.

nodes.name: Epstein's 1994 New Albany house
nodes.note: House Epstein bought in New Albany, Ohio in 1994, about half a mile from the Wexner home (Axios Columbus, citing property records).

nodes.name: L Brands (The Limited)
nodes.note: Retail group Les Wexner founded; parent of Victoria's Secret. Wexner stepped down as chairman in 2020 after investor pressure over his Epstein ties.

nodes.name: House Oversight deposition of Les Wexner (18 Feb 2026)
nodes.note: Deposition held at Wexner's New Albany home after January subpoenas to Wexner, Indyke and Kahn. NBC4 reported he paid Epstein about $200 million over the years; that figure needs the transcript.

nodes.name: Survivors' suit v. Wexner, the Wexner Foundation and Nine East 71st Street Corp. (2026)
nodes.note: Civil suit by eleven women in New York Supreme Court, reported 1 April 2026 (filed 30 March; one report says 6 March), later moved toward federal court. Alleges Wexner and the foundation paid Epstein $200M+ (1987–2007), that the Nine East townhouse and a plane were transferred, under the Gender-Motivated Violence Act. Allegations only; Wexner has not been charged and a spokesperson expressed sympathy for the victims.

nodes.name: Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation (Dubai)
nodes.note: Dubai government body that runs the emirate's ports and free zones. Bin Sulayem chaired it; Dubai's ruler decreed a new chairman on 13 Feb 2026.

nodes.name: April 2009 email: "I loved the torture video"
nodes.note: On 24 April 2009 Epstein wrote "where are you? are you ok, I loved the torture video" to an address the DOJ had redacted; Reps. Massie and Khanna identified it as bin Sulayem's on 10 Feb 2026. The recipient replied that he was in China. The video is unidentified and no criminal allegation has been made against bin Sulayem; US officials say appearing in the files is not indicative of wrongdoing.

nodes.name: Bank of New York Mellon
nodes.note: Custodian bank. Senate Finance (Wyden) opened a probe in 2026 into hundreds of millions of dollars moved through BNY accounts for Epstein. A federal judge dismissed the Jane Doe class action against BNY on 29 Jan 2026; plaintiffs said they would appeal. BNY says it had no involvement in Epstein's crimes.

nodes.name: Senate Finance report "Looking the Other Way" (4 Aug 2026)
nodes.note: 67-page report by Sen. Ron Wyden's Democratic staff after a four-year investigation. Says Bank of America likely violated anti-money-laundering law by failing to report $170M from Leon Black to Epstein, that JPMorgan executives coached Epstein on withdrawing cash through shell companies, and that 13 bankers at JPMorgan, Bank of America and Deutsche Bank merit investigation. A staff report, not a ruling.

nodes.name: Judge Jed Rakoff
nodes.note: Federal judge in Manhattan overseeing the Jane Doe class actions: dismissed the BNY case (29 Jan 2026), let two claims against Bank of America proceed, and approved its $72.5M settlement.

nodes.name: Jane Doe v. Bank of America and BNY (SDNY, filed 15 Oct 2025)
nodes.note: Proposed class actions by a Florida woman for Epstein victims. BNY dismissed 29 Jan 2026 (appeal planned); Bank of America settled for $72.5M, finally approved; earlier class settlements were JPMorgan $290M and Deutsche Bank $75M.

nodes.name: NPA clause on victims' counsel (Dec 2007–Sept 2008)
nodes.note: Draft agreement language to appoint a guardian ad litem for up to 40 identified victims. Files released in January 2026 show Kirkland's Jay Lefkowitz asked the US Attorney's Office to remove it, then threatened to take it "to Washington." When Epstein signed, the legal-representation section had changed. DOJ's own 11 Dec 2007 letter to Lefkowitz says the agreement gave its Office the exclusive right to choose that attorney.

nodes.name: Reid Weingarten
nodes.note: Washington defense lawyer (Steptoe) reported on Epstein's 2008 defense team. Role not yet confirmed from a primary document.

nodes.name: Gerald Lefcourt
nodes.note: New York defense lawyer reported on Epstein's 2008 defense team. Role not yet confirmed from a primary document.

nodes.name: Guy Lewis
nodes.note: Former US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, reported on Epstein's 2008 defense team. Role not yet confirmed from a primary document.

nodes.name: Steptoe & Johnson
nodes.note: Law firm of Reid Weingarten; link to Epstein not yet confirmed from a primary document.

nodes.name: Edwards Henderson (Bradley Edwards)
nodes.note: Law firm of Bradley Edwards, who represented victims in the Crime Victims' Rights Act challenge to the 2008 non-prosecution agreement. Role to be confirmed against the docket.
